[Jump to content](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#bodyContent) From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia [![](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/Population_by_U.S._state.svg/250px-Population_by_U.S._state.svg.png)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Population_by_U.S._state.svg) Resident population of each [U.S. state](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state"), the [District of Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C."), and [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico") in 2024 according to the [U.S. Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Census_Bureau "U.S. Census Bureau") The [states and territories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_states_and_territories_of_the_United_States "List of states and territories of the United States") included in the [United States Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau")'s statistics for the United States population, ethnicity, and most other categories include the [50 states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") and [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.") Separate statistics are maintained for the five permanently inhabited [territories of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territories_of_the_United_States "Territories of the United States"): [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico"), [Guam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guam "Guam"), the [U.S. Virgin Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Virgin_Islands "United States Virgin Islands"), [American Samoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Samoa "American Samoa"), and the [Northern Mariana Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Mariana_Islands "Northern Mariana Islands").[\[1\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-1) As of April 1, 2020, the date of the [2020 United States census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), the nine most populous [U.S. states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") contain slightly more than half of the total population. The 25 least populous states contain less than one-sixth of the total population. [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California"), the most populous state, contains more people than the 21 least populous states combined, and [Wyoming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wyoming "Wyoming"), the least populous state, has a population less than any of the 31 most populous U.S. cities. ## Method \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population&action=edit§ion=1 "Edit section: Method")\] The [United States Census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census "United States Census") counts the persons residing in the [United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States "United States") including [citizens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Citizenship "Citizenship"), non-citizen [permanent residents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permanent_residence_(United_States) "Permanent residence (United States)") and non-citizen long-term visitors.[\[2\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-2) Civilian and military federal employees serving abroad and their dependents are counted in their home state.[\[3\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-3) ## Electoral apportionment \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population&action=edit§ion=2 "Edit section: Electoral apportionment")\] Every 10 years, the [U.S. Census Bureau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Census_Bureau "United States Census Bureau") is charged with making an actual count of all residents by state and territory. The accuracy of this count is then tested after the fact, and sometimes statistically significant undercounts or overcounts occur. For example, for the [2020 decennial census](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_United_States_census "2020 United States census"), 14 states had significant miscounts ranging from 1.5% to 6.6%. While these adjustments may be reflected in government programs over the following decade, the 10-year representative apportionments discussed below are not changed to reflect the miscount.[\[4\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-4) ### House of Representatives \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population&action=edit§ion=3 "Edit section: House of Representatives")\] Based on this decennial census, each state is allocated a portion of the 435 fixed seats in the [United States House of Representatives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives") (until the early 20th century, the apportionment process generally increased the size of the House based on the results of the census until the size of the House was capped by the [Reapportionment Act of 1929](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reapportionment_Act_of_1929 "Reapportionment Act of 1929")), with each state guaranteed at least one Representative. The [allocation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_congressional_apportionment "United States congressional apportionment") is based on each state's proportion of the combined population of the [fifty states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._state "U.S. state") (not including the [District of Columbia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/District_of_Columbia "District of Columbia"), [Guam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guam "Guam"), [American Samoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Samoa "American Samoa"), the [Northern Mariana Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Mariana_Islands "Northern Mariana Islands"), [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico"), or the [U.S. Virgin Islands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Virgin_Islands "United States Virgin Islands")). ### Electoral College \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population&action=edit§ion=4 "Edit section: Electoral College")\] The [Electoral College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Electoral_College "United States Electoral College"), every four years, elects the [President](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") and [Vice President of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_President_of_the_United_States "Vice President of the United States") based on the popular vote in each state and the District of Columbia. Each state's number of votes in the Electoral College is equal to its number of members in the Senate plus members in the House of Representatives.[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-auto-5) The [Twenty-third Amendment to the United States Constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twenty-third_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "Twenty-third Amendment to the United States Constitution") additionally grants the District of Columbia (D.C.), which is not a state, as many Electoral College votes as it would have if it _were_ a state, while having no more votes than the least populous state (Wyoming). Since the U.S. Constitution guarantees every state at least one member of the U.S. House of Representatives and two members of the U.S. Senate, every state has at least three Electoral College votes. Thus, the Electoral College has 538 members (100 [senators](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate"), plus 435 representatives due to the limit imposed by the Reapportionment Act of 1929, plus 3 members for the District of Columbia).[\[5\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-auto-5) [Territories of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Territories_of_the_United_States "Territories of the United States") are not included in the Electoral College: people in those territories cannot vote directly for the President of the United States,[\[6\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-6) although they may participate in the partisan nominating primaries and caucuses.[\[7\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-7) ## State and territory rankings \[ [edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population&action=edit§ion=5 "Edit section: State and territory rankings")\] | State or territory | Census population[\[8\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-CensusEst2025-8)[\[9\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-Census2020-9)[\[a\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-residentundercount-11) | Largest cities | [House seats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives")[\[b\]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_U.S._states_and_territories_by_population#cite_note-12) | Pop. per

By far the most populous state in the United States is California, which has nearly 40
million residents and comprises nearly 12% of the country’s total population. If
California were a country, it would have the [fourth or fifth largest economy in the world](https://www.bloomberg.com/opinion/articles/2022-10-24/california-poised-to-overtake-germany-as-world-s-no-4-economy) and the 38th-highest population, ahead of countries including [Canada](https://worldpopulationreview.com/countries/canada), [Australia](https://worldpopulationreview.com/countries/australia), [Peru](https://worldpopulationreview.com/countries/peru), and [Greece](https://worldpopulationreview.com/countries/greece).

[Texas](https://worldpopulationreview.com/states/texas) has the second-largest population of any US state, with more than
30 million residents (9% of the US total) as of 2023. Moreover, Texas has a growth rate of
1.34% per year, while California’s growth rate is notably lower at 0.57%. The impact of such
differing growth rates is obvious when viewed over time: Since 2010, the population of Texas
has increased by more than 20%, while California has grown just under 12%.

The third-most-populated state in the US is [Florida](https://worldpopulationreview.com/states/florida), with a
population of more than 22.3 million and a growth rate of 1.24% per year, and the state of [New York](https://worldpopulationreview.com/states/new-york) ranks fourth. About half of the 20.40 million people who live in the state of New York reside
in [New York](https://worldpopulationreview.com/us-cities/new-york/new-york). It is notable that the three most
populous states in the US are among the top ten [states with the longest coastlines](https://worldpopulationreview.com/state-rankings/coastline-length-by-state), and both California and Texas are among the largest states in the union by [land area](https://worldpopulationreview.com/state-rankings/states-by-area).

States in [New England](https://worldpopulationreview.com/state-rankings/new-england-states),
along the Northeast seaboard, tend to be quite small geographically but with higher
populations. [Rhode Island](https://worldpopulationreview.com/states/rhode-island) (pop. 1,110,822) is the [smallest state by land area](https://worldpopulationreview.com/state-rankings/states-by-area), but it has a higher population than many larger states, including [Alaska](https://worldpopulationreview.com/states/alaska) (740,339), both [North Dakota](https://worldpopulationreview.com/states/north-dakota) and [South Dakota](https://worldpopulationreview.com/states/south-dakota) (811,044 and 908,414, respectively), and [Wyoming](https://worldpopulationreview.com/states/wyoming) (580,817).

### Population Distribution

The population of the United States is distributed unevenly across the 50 states,
Washington DC, and territories such as Puerto Rico. States on the country's border tend to
be the most populous, whether they be located on the [West Coast](https://worldpopulationreview.com/state-rankings/west-coast-states) (California), the [East Coast](https://worldpopulationreview.com/state-rankings/east-coast-states) (New York, Florida, arguably Pennsylvania), or the southern border (Texas, Florida again).
Conversely, interior states such as those in the [Great Plains](https://worldpopulationreview.com/state-rankings/great-plains-states) and [Midwest](https://worldpopulationreview.com/state-rankings/midwest-states) tend to be less populous.
However, exceptions do exist—for example, the [Great Lakes](https://worldpopulationreview.com/state-rankings/great-lakes-states) state of [Illinois](https://worldpopulationreview.com/states/illinois) has the sixth-largest population of any state despite
its Midwestern location.

Most states in the US are currently experiencing population growth. The greatest rate of
growth belongs to Florida (2.0%), followed by Texas (1.8%) and Utah (1.72%). By
comparison, the state with the lowest population growth is [Vermont](https://worldpopulationreview.com/states/vermont),
whose population shrank by 0.03%.

[District of Columbia](https://worldpopulationreview.com/states/district-of-columbia), or Washington, D.C., is not
a state. It is a federal district — specifically, the District of Columbia — which serves as
the capital of the United States. The U.S. Constitution dictates that the federal district
be under the jurisdiction of the U.S. Congress. While it functions as a state in many
respects, including operating its own school system and managing certain federal programs,
it lacks full voting representation in Congress and is not considered a state

[Puerto Rico](https://worldpopulationreview.com/states/puerto-rico) is also not a state; it is a territory of the United
States. Specifically, it's an unincorporated territory, meaning it's part of the U.S. but not
fully integrated as a state. Puerto Rico is often referred to as a commonwealth.

### About the Population Clock and Population Estimates

#### U.S. Population

The U.S. population clock is based on a series of short-term projections for the resident population of the United States. This includes people whose usual residence is in the 50 states and the District of Columbia. These projections do not include members of the Armed Forces overseas, their dependents, or other U.S. citizens residing outside the United States.

The projections are based on a monthly series of population estimates starting with the April 1, 2020 resident population from the 2020 Census.

At the end of each year, a revised series of population estimates from the census date forward is used to update the short-term projections for the population clock. Once the updated series of monthly projections is completed, the daily population clock values are derived by interpolation. Within each calendar month, the daily numerical population change is assumed to be constant, subject to negligible differences caused by rounding.

Population estimates produced by the U.S. Census Bureau for the United States, states, metropolitan and micropolitan statistical areas, counties, cities, towns, as well as for Puerto Rico and its municipios can be found on the [Population Estimates](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/popest.html) web page. Projections of the future population for the United States can be found on the [Population Projections](https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/popproj.html) web page.

Cities featured on the Most Populous and Highest Density lists feature populations of 5,000 or more on July 1, 2023.
